## One prompt, a full investigation

```text
Reverse engineer the Notes app. Find how offline search works, explain it,
and build a version for my project using TypeScript and SQLite.

## CLI

The agent workflow above is the easiest way to use REA. For a one-off overview from the Terminal:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze /Applications/Notes.app

When REA feeds a shell pipeline, enable `pipefail` so a downstream formatter
cannot hide its failure:

```bash
set -o pipefail
rea inventory-artifact ./app.asar --json | jq . > inventory.json

Capture a scenario or compare two saved Process Capture v4 Evidence records:

```bash
rea capture-process ./scenario.json > authority.json
usecases: Investigate a feature you like and build a version tailored to your own product.

outputs: Record every successful result as deterministic Evidence v2 with artifact and provider identity, confidence, authority, limitations, and locations.
ordered events return typed decisions, actions, captured aliases, transition journals, final state, and exact limit use without echoing request or captured values.

The comparison reports each observed dimension separately and identifies the
first terminal, interaction, exit, filesystem, protocol, process, or shim
divergence.
Build bounded function dossiers with pseudocode, assembly, CFG edges, comments, calls, references, strings, and names.
`rea doctor --json` is read-only and distinguishes unsupported hosts, missing dependencies, a missing local analysis engine, configuration drift, and healthy checks.
Validate finite replay machines without launching a target through `run_replay_machine` or `rea run-replay-machine`;

Integrity failures identify the logical
path, declared and calculated SHA-256 values, and whether the entry was
unpacked
reliability: It does not claim to recover original source code or automatically clone an application.
Analysis runs on your supported local host. REA does not upload the app to a hosted analysis service.
provider failures never trigger transparent fallback.
An analysis timeout, scan or inventory safety limit, request timeout, or oversized response fails explicitly instead of returning a partial result labeled complete.
Exports never replace an existing file unless `--overwrite` is explicit. Imports are size/depth bounded, validate every Evidence v2 ID and manifest, and never execute bundle content.

Snapshot files can contain proprietary analysis
results and local paths, so REA keeps them local, writes them with owner-only
permissions, and requires a separate approved root:
Query values, credentials, cookies, authorization headers, storage values, and raw JSON or WebSocket values are never retained.

Automation has no default
grant: use the shared project/session policy, or set
`REA_BROWSER_SCENARIO_AUTO_GRANT=true` only for a trusted unattended
environment.
REA reports timeouts and remediation through CLI or MCP results instead of attempting to answer UI prompts.
If shutdown or cleanup cannot be verified, `close_binary` returns `cleanup_incomplete` with the affected local resources.
